hints.title: Maintain Frequency and Count of Frequencies
hints.text: Keep track of the frequency of each number and how many distinct numbers share each frequency.

hints.title: Verify Removability Conditions
hints.text: Removing one element is valid if all frequencies are one, or if one frequency exceeds others by one, or one count is one.

hints.title: Scan from Left to Right
hints.text: Evaluate validity after incorporating each element from index 0 to n - 1, recording the largest valid prefix length.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
from collections import Counter

class Solution:
    def maxEqualFreq(self, nums: list[int]) -> int:
        count = Counter()
        freq = Counter()
        max_f = 0
        ans = 0
        
        for i, x in enumerate(nums):
            if count[x] > 0:
                freq[count[x]] -= 1
            count[x] += 1
            freq[count[x]] += 1
            max_f = max(max_f, count[x])
            
            # Conditions for validity:
            # 1. max_f == 1 (all elements distinct)
            # 2. freq[max_f] * max_f + 1 == i + 1 (one element with freq 1, others with max_f)
            # 3. (freq[max_f - 1] + 1) * (max_f - 1) + 1 == i + 1 and freq[max_f] == 1
            if max_f == 1:
                ans = i + 1
            elif freq[max_f] * max_f + 1 == i + 1 and freq[1] == 1:
                ans = i + 1
            elif freq[max_f] == 1 and (freq[max_f - 1] + 1) * (max_f - 1) + 1 == i + 1:
                ans = i + 1
                
        return ans
```

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Rechecking all frequencies from scratch at every prefix requires O(N^2) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Dual frequency tracking maps allow O(1) condition checks per element.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should enumerate all valid equal-frequency configurations after a single deletion.
